claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, provided the unresolved small-business onboarding limitation is disclosed in the model card and the draft runbook is treated only as draft monitoring support rather than a closed mitigation.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows small-business onboarding is a named launch use case and the limitation will be disclosed before launch, the actor's position would move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or risk acceptance satisfying the policy fields, the certification basis would strengthen materially.
If evidence shows the issue is not a named launch use case or not material, the disclosure-based rationale would weaken and the actor's policy claim would need revision.
If the launch proceeds without disclosure and without approved mitigation or risk acceptance, the position would move toward noncompliant.
evidence_requests: Evidence that small-business onboarding is a named launch use case for this release.
A materiality determination or equivalent approval showing the unresolved slice issue qualifies as a material limitation.
Any approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation record containing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The final model-card text or approval showing the limitation will in fact be disclosed before launch.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, but it also shows an unresolved below-target slice and only a draft mitigation with owner and threshold still TBD.
The record does not show an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, so the runbook cannot remove any current disclosure obligation under the stated policy.

The actor's recommendation depends on treating the small-business onboarding issue as a material limitation for a named launch use case, but the available evidence does not directly establish that named-use-case predicate or formal materiality determination.
The recommendation is only supportable as a caveated certification posture tied to disclosure; a clean certification conclusion would conflict with the policy text.
unsupported_claims: Release policy requires disclosure here as a matter of established fact; the record shows the policy rule, but does not directly prove that this specific issue is formally classified as a material limitation for a named launch use case.

The evidence supports certification more strongly with explicit disclosure than with any other disposition; this is plausible, but remains partly judgmental because the packet lacks approved mitigation or explicit risk-acceptance evidence.
